hits.section: Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › Temperament Spec
hits.text:
Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › Temperament Spec
Temperament | Responds to | If you are Heroes | If you are a Menace |
Idealist | Help. Refuses bribes. | Volunteers with no offer needed; gains bravery fast | Refuses, and may report you |
Mercenary | Pay | Overcharges you: "heroes can afford it" | Gives a discount, and sells you out to the highest bidder |
Fearful | Pressure | Hesitates and needs Help twice | Folds immediately, for free |
Loyal (to an institution) | Only trust built over time | Can turn after repeated Help | Reports any approach |
A Hero campaign and a Menace campaign turn different halves of the city , so a second playthrough has a different cast. That's the replay value.

hits.section: Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › What a person is made of Spec (1/2)
hits.text:
Knowledge makes consent cheap. Reputation decides who says yes. › What a person is made of Spec
Every number about a person reads as a word, so the dossier never shows a bare score:
Bravery: informant · helper · accomplice · fighter. Resentment: compliant · resentful · informer.
Fear: calm · uneasy · afraid · terrified. Loyalty (to the cell): none · obliged · trusting · sworn. In the Talker test, loyalty means loyalty to the cell; loyalty to an employer or to the civic order is what the Loyal temperament is.
At the start everyone is at the bottom of every scale, except that an Idealist starts one step braver (helper) and a Fearful person starts uneasy, so they talk when questioned until someone helps them.
One clear need from a closed list: debt, cash, housing, papers, kin, care, protection, advancement or a secret. Each can be met by Help or Pressure. Once a need is met, a new one appears between missions, drawn from the person's own stream so it replays; a turned contact tells you it free in the debrief, and anyone else has to be listened to again.

faults.fault: Temperament fit, loyal read line 3: "Reports any approach." The Temperament Spec says a Loyal person reports any approach only when the cell is a Menace. Under a Hero campaign the Loyal "Can turn after repeated Help". As a general statement the Scout's read misleads the player: this is the same flaw just fixed in the idealist read. Line 2 ("Trust comes slowly.") already gives the true read.
faults.fix: Drop the absolute, e.g. "Won't be rushed. Help, and keep helping." or "May report a stranger's offer."
